category_specific_evidence: np.quantile computes weights.cumsum(..., dtype=np.float64) then normalizes via cdf /= cdf[-1, ...] (normalization to 1).
When weights are all zeros, cdf[-1] is zero, so normalization produces invalid values (RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in divide) and the reported output is array(1).
The code checks for NaN in the final cdf after normalization: if np.isnan(cdf[-1]).any() it raises ValueError("Weights included NaN, inf or were all zero.").
The issue repro calls: np.quantile([1,2,3,4], 0.5, weights=[0,0,0,0], method='inverted_cdf').
The PR body states quantile should error when weights are all zeros, and also when at least one weight is np.nan or np.inf.
reproduction_risks: Using inputs that do not trigger the 'weights all zero' / NaN / inf path may not reproduce the bug.
Different quantile methods (the repro uses method='inverted_cdf') might change which internal path is exercised; the evidence specifically mentions the inverted_cdf method in the repro.
